sourcePolicy: Primary public sources only; retain source date, scope, denominator, implementation state and project-specific unknowns.

claims.claim: SB6 was signed and became effective June 20, 2025.
claims.recheckTrigger: Amending legislation or a change in the operative statutory provisions.

claims.claim: Adopted §25.194 was filed September 18, published October 2 and effective October 8, 2026. Applicability covers specified non-energized single-site new loads, expansions and co-location; incremental additions are the relevant expansion scope.
claims.recheckTrigger: Amendment, litigation affecting applicability, or transaction-specific grandfathering claim. Do not reuse March 2026 proposal thresholds or fee structure.

claims.claim: Intermediate study fee $100,000; intermediate security $50,000/MW requested or incremental demand. SLLIA security is greater of $50,000/MW contracted demand or allocated system-upgrade costs. Direct-interconnection costs use cash CIAC; prior security may be credited under the rule.
claims.recheckTrigger: Rule inflation adjustments, subsequent tariff/cost-allocation rules, SLLIA adoption, or actual project agreements and credit instruments.

claims.claim: ERCOT reported approximately 474 GW of large-load interconnection requests using June 2026 information; about 90% data centers. These are requests, not operational power or guaranteed construction.
claims.units: GW requested; percent of large-load request capacity by project type
claims.recheckTrigger: New ERCOT request, verification, allocation or realized-load report. Do not label this October 2026 operating demand.

claims.claim: April 15 preliminary forecast reported approximately 367,790 MW demand by 2032. ERCOT described it as higher than expected future growth and not a prediction of what would be built.

sources.status: preliminary planning snapshot; expressly not latest forecast in article

claims.units: MW demand in the ERCOT region by forecast year 2032
claims.recheckTrigger: Verified revised long-term forecast. Do not subtract a queue snapshot from forecast demand to estimate spare capacity.

claims.claim: ERCOT described an August 3 Batch Zero pause and delayed final classification, then issued conditional classifications September 3 subject to verification/model cures/possible exceptions. December 10 was the August presentation’s planned eligibility-report date.

sources.status: agency process update; future dates are planned
conditional classifications issued; not energization approval

claims.recheckTrigger: Final eligibility report, project condition resolution, new exception or energization notice.

claims.claim: September 9 eligibility RFI required complete responses within 10 business days of individual issuance; extension request no more than 5 business days. Failed or incomplete verification can exclude a load from Batch Zero.
claims.recheckTrigger: Supplemental RFIs, extension confirmation, verification outcome or a new notice changing the deadline.

claims.claim: Separate September 14 RFI covered specified conditional Batch Zero data centers and specified substantiated 25-to-under-75-MW facilities. Responses due October 12 at 5 p.m. CPT; report expected no later than December 10. Section C water questions issued for TWDB may carry Water Code consequences for incomplete responses.

sources.status: RFI issued; deadline stated; report planned

claims.recheckTrigger: Deadline extension or subsequent notice, new classifications, December report or agency Water Code interpretation. Do not turn expected report publication into a connection approval.

claims.claim: Governor directed TCEQ September 21 to halt data-center permits until ERCOT audit completion and requested a compliance update by October 19.

sources.status: governmental directive; no project outcome established

claims.recheckTrigger: October 19 compliance update, audit completion, directive amendment, TCEQ implementation or a specific permit decision.

claims.claim: SB6 distinguishes post-December-31-2025 transmission-voltage firm-load-shed protocols with critical-load exceptions from a >=75-MW demand-management service with a 24-hour notice provision. §25.521 published August 14 was proposed; September ERCOT report described implementation as in progress. No service revenue is assumed.

sources.status: proposed §25.521; not treated as effective terms

claims.recheckTrigger: Final adoption and effective date, implemented ERCOT protocols and actual program participation/procurement notices. Public retrieval of the PUCT project page failed; do not claim final adoption was exhaustively ruled out.

claims.claim: SB6 addresses new co-located loads at specified existing stand-alone generators; ERCOT’s July example distinguishes existing from new co-located generation. SB6 section 6 required transmission-cost-recovery review and rules by December 31, 2026; this deadline does not determine a buyer’s tariff.
claims.recheckTrigger: Co-location decision for the actual project, amended rules, December cost-recovery rules, current utility tariffs.

claims.claim: Two hypothetical 80-MW allocations: Site A requests 100 MW, gives $5m intermediate security and $6m SLLIA security on assumed $6m upgrades; Site B requests 80 MW, gives $4m intermediate and SLLIA security on assumed $3m upgrades. Assumed CIAC $3m/$4.2m. 18 months × $150k = $2.7m delay sensitivity. 80 MW × 70% × 8,760 h = 490,560 MWh; × assumed $65/MWh = $31,886,400 supply expense.

sources.status: formula source only; every project and price input explicitly illustrative

claims.status: calculated illustration, not observed project data or tariff forecast
claims.recheckTrigger: Any changed rule formula or input. Preserve explicit assumptions, do not add intermediate and SLLIA security, and do not label supply-only calculation total delivered cost.
